text: Let f : R $\to$ R be a continuous function such that $f(3x)-f(x)=x$. If $f(8)=7$, then $f(14)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $g(x)=f(x)-\dfrac{x}{2}$. Then

$g(3x)-g(x)=f(3x)-f(x)-\frac{3x}{2}+\frac{x}{2}=x-x=0$

so $g(x)=g\left (\dfrac{x}{3}\right )$, and repeating, $g(x)=g\left (\dfrac{x}{3^{n}}\right )$ for every $n$.

As $n\to \infty$, $\dfrac{x}{3^{n}}\to 0$, and continuity of $g$ gives $g(x)=g(0)=c$, a constant. So $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}+c$.

From $f(8)=4+c=7$, $c=3$, so

$f(14)=\frac{14}{2}+3=10$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: The odd natural number a, such that the area of the region bounded by $y = 1, y = 3, x = 0, x = y^{a}$ is $\frac{364}{3}$, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{a}$ is an odd natural number and

$\left |\int\limits _{1}^{3}y^{a}dy\right |=\frac{364}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\frac{1}{a+1}\left (y^{a+1}\right )_{1}^{3}\right |=\frac{364}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3^{a+1}-1}{a+1}=\pm \frac{364}{3}$

Solving with $(-)$ sign,

$\frac{3^{a+1}-1}{a+1}=\frac{364}{3}\Rightarrow (a=5)$

Solving with $(+)$ sign,

$\frac{3^{a+1}-1}{a+1}=\frac{-364}{3}$, No a exist

$\therefore$ $(a=5)$

for continuity at $x=0$

text: If $\frac{dy}{dx}+2y\tan x=\sin x,0<x<\frac{π}{2}$ and $y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$, then the maximum value of $y(x)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+2y\tan x=\sin x$

which is a first order linear differential equation.

Integrating factor (I. F.) $=e^{\int 2\tan xdx}$

$=e^{2\ln |\sec x|}=\sec ^{2}x$

Solution of differential equation can be written as

$y~.\quad \sec ^{2}x=\int \sin x\qquad .\sec ^{2}xdx=\int \sec x.\tan xdx$

$y\sec ^{2}x=\sec x+C$

$y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0,0=\sec \frac{π}{3}+C\Rightarrow C=-2$

$y=\frac{\sec x-2}{\sec ^{2}x}=\cos x-2\cos ^{2}x$

$=\frac{1}{8}-2\left (\cos x-\frac{1}{4}\right )^{2}$

$y_{\max }=\frac{1}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: A point $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points $(1,2)$ and $(-2,1)$ is 14. Let $f(x,y)=0$ be the locus of $\mathrm{P}$, which intersects the $x$-axis at the points $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{B}$ and the $y$-axis at the points C, D. Then the area of the quadrilateral ACBD is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let point $P:(h,k)$

$(h-1)^{2}+(k-2)^{2}+(h+2)^{2}+(k-1)^{2}=14$

$2h^{2}+2k^{2}+2h-6k-4=0$

Locus of $P:x^{2}+y^{2}+x-3y-2=0$

Intersection with x-axis,

$x^{2}+x-2=0$

$\Rightarrow x=-2,1$

Intersection with y-axis,

$y^{2}-3y-2=0$

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{3\pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$

Area of the quadrilateral ACBD is

$=\frac{1}{2}(|x_{1}|+|x_{2}|)(|y_{1}|+|y_{2}|)$

$=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times \sqrt{17}=\frac{3\sqrt{17}}{2}$

text: Let $\mathrm{E}_{1},\mathrm{E}_{2},\mathrm{E}_{3}$ be three mutually exclusive events such that $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{E}_{1})=\frac{2+3\mathrm{p}}{6},\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{E}_{2})=\frac{2-\mathrm{p}}{8}$ and $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{E}_{3})=\frac{1-\mathrm{p}}{2}$. If the maximum and minimum values of $\mathrm{p}$ are $\mathrm{p}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{p}_{2}$, then $(\mathrm{p}_{1}+\mathrm{p}_{2})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each probability lies in $[0,1]$:

$0\leq \dfrac{2+3p}{6}\leq 1\Rightarrow -\dfrac{2}{3}\leq p\leq \dfrac{4}{3}$

$0\leq \dfrac{2-p}{8}\leq 1\Rightarrow -6\leq p\leq 2$

$0\leq \dfrac{1-p}{2}\leq 1\Rightarrow -1\leq p\leq 1$

For mutually exclusive events, $P(E_{1})+P(E_{2})+P(E_{3})=P(E_{1}\cup E_{2}\cup E_{3})\leq 1$:

$\dfrac{2+3p}{6}+\dfrac{2-p}{8}+\dfrac{1-p}{2}=\dfrac{26-3p}{24}\leq 1\Rightarrow p\geq \dfrac{2}{3}$

Combining, $\dfrac{2}{3}\leq p\leq 1$, so $p_{1}=1$ and $p_{2}=\dfrac{2}{3}$.

$p_{1}+p_{2}=1+\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{5}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: The number of distinct real roots of the equation $x^{5}\left (x^{3}-x^{2}-x+1\right )+x\left (3x^{3}-4x^{2}-2x+4\right )-1=0$ is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{8}-x^{7}-x^{6}+x^{5}+3x^{4}-4x^{3}-2x^{2}+4x-1=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{7}(x-1)-x^{5}(x-1)+3x^{3}(x-1)-x(x^{2}-1)+2x(1-x)+(x-1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x^{7}-x^{5}+3x^{3}-x(x+1)-2x+1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x^{7}-x^{5}+3x^{3}-x^{2}-3x+1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x^{5}(x^{2}-1)+3x(x^{2}-1)-1(x^{2}-1))=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x^{2}-1)(x^{5}+3x-1)=0$

$\therefore$ $x=\pm 1$ are roots of above equation and $x^{5}+3x-1$ is a monotonic term hence vanishs at exactly one value of x other than 1 or $-$1.

$\therefore$ 3 real roots.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: The equations of the sides $\mathrm{AB},\mathrm{BC}$ and $\mathrm{CA}$ of a triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$ are $2x+y=0,x+\mathrm{p}y=15\mathrm{a}$ and $x-y=3$ respectively. If its orthocentre is $(2,a),-\frac{1}{2}<\mathrm{a}<2$, then $\mathrm{p}$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Vertex A is the intersection of $2x+y=0$ and $x-y=3$, so $A=(1,-2)$.

$AH⟂BC$: slope of $AH=\dfrac{a+2}{2-1}=a+2$ and slope of $BC=-\dfrac{1}{p}$, so $(a+2)\left (-\dfrac{1}{p}\right )=-1\Rightarrow p=a+2$, i.e. $a=p-2$.

Vertex C: putting $x=y+3$ in $x+py=15a$ gives $y=\dfrac{15a-3}{p+1}=\dfrac{15p-33}{p+1}$ and $x=y+3=\dfrac{18p-30}{p+1}$.

$CH⟂AB$, and $AB$ has slope $-2$, so the slope of $CH$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{15p-33}{p+1}-(p-2)}{\dfrac{18p-30}{p+1}-2}=\dfrac{15p-33-(p-2)(p+1)}{16p-32}=\dfrac{-p^{2}+16p-31}{16p-32}=\dfrac{1}{2}$

$-2p^{2}+32p-62=16p-32\Rightarrow p^{2}-8p+15=0\Rightarrow p=3\text{or}5$

$p=5$ gives $a=3$, outside $-\dfrac{1}{2}<a<2$; $p=3$ gives $a=1$, which is allowed.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: Let the function $f(x)=2x^{2}-\log _{\mathrm{e}}x,x>0$, be decreasing in $(0,\mathrm{a})$ and increasing in $(\mathrm{a},4)$. A tangent to the parabola $y^{2}=4ax$ at a point $\mathrm{P}$ on it passes through the point $(8\mathrm{a},8\mathrm{a}-1)$ but does not pass through the point $\left (-\frac{1}{a},0\right )$. If the equation of the normal at $P$ is : $\frac{x}{α}+\frac{y}{β}=1$, then $α+β$ is equal to $________________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f^{'}(x)=\frac{4x^{2}-1}{x}$ so f(x) is decreasing in $\left (0,\frac{1}{2}\right )$ and increasing in $\left (\frac{1}{2},\infty \right )\Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{2}$

Tangent at $y^{2}=2x\Rightarrow y=mx+\frac{1}{2m}$

It is passing through $(4,3)$

$3=4m+\frac{1}{2m}\Rightarrow m=\frac{1}{2}$ or $\frac{1}{4}$

So tangent may be

$y=\frac{1}{2}x+1$ or $y=\frac{1}{4}x+2$

But $y=\frac{1}{2}x+1$ passes through $(-2,0)$ so rejected.

Equation of normal

$y=-4x-2\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )(-4)-\frac{1}{2}(-4)^{3}$

or $y=-4x+4+32$

or $\frac{x}{9}+\frac{y}{36}=1$
